title.narrative: Restoration through Science-based Execution and Established Biodiverse Registry for Degraded Ecosystems in Protected Areas and Broader Landscapes in the Philippines (RESEEDPh)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The RESEEDPH project is designed to deliver multiple socio-economic benefits, enhancing the wellbeing of local communities while ensuring environmental sustainability and climate resilience. These benefits are embedded in the project’s restoration and conservation efforts and will be monitored and reported on throughout implementation, including at the Mid-Term Review (MTR) and Terminal Evaluation (TE). 1. Climate Security and Disaster ResilienceThe project directly contributes to climate security by enhancing forest cover, improving carbon sequestration, and promoting agroforestry systems that mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The restoration of degraded landscapes in Catanduanes, Bohol, and the North Cotabato portion of Mt. Apo Natural Park will help stabilize local microclimates and reduce the risk of climate-induced disasters such as flooding, drought, and typhoon-induced landslides. By implementing nature-based solutions, such as watershed rehabilitation and soil conservation practices, communities will be better equipped to withstand extreme weather events. 2. Water Security and Watershed ProtectionHealthy forests and restored ecosystems play a critical role in regulating water cycles and ensuring sustainable water supply for communities. By restoring forested areas and watersheds, the project will enhance groundwater recharge, improve water retention, and reduce sedimentation in rivers and streams. This is particularly vital in upland agricultural areas and communities reliant on clean and accessible water sources for irrigation and daily consumption. Improved watershed health will secure water resources for local populations, particularly during dry seasons. 3. Food Security and Sustainable AgricultureThrough agroforestry, soil restoration, and biodiversity-friendly enterprises (BDFEs), the project will promote sustainable food production systems that benefit farming households. Integrating native tree species, fruit-bearing crops, and climate-resilient agricultural practices will help diversify food sources and increase productivity. By promoting landscape-level restoration and sustainable farming techniques, the project ensures long-term food security while protecting natural ecosystems from further degradation. 4. Health Benefits from Ecosystem RestorationThe project’s restoration efforts will help improve air and water quality, reducing pollution-related health risks for local populations. Forest conservation and agro-biodiversity initiatives will reduce exposure to environmental hazards such as soil erosion, water contamination, and heat stress in deforested areas. Additionally, by promoting nutrient-rich indigenous crops and sustainable farming practices, the project can enhance community nutrition and support healthier diets among vulnerable populations, particularly in rural areas. 5. Sustainability of Livelihoods and Economic EmpowermentOne of the core goals of the RESEEDPH project is to create sustainable livelihood opportunities for forest-dependent communities, farmers, and indigenous peoples. The project will introduce alternative income-generating activities, such as agroforestry, eco-tourism, and biodiversity-friendly enterprises (BDFEs), which will provide long-term economic stability. The introduction of market linkages, training programs, and policy support will ensure that communities are equipped with the knowledge and resources to sustain these livelihoods beyond the project’s lifespan. 6. Reduced Vulnerabilities and Social InclusionThe project incorporates social protection mechanisms and community-driven approaches to ensure that marginalized groups, including women, youth, and indigenous communities, actively participate in restoration activities. By integrating DSWD’s poverty alleviation programs, cash-for-work initiatives, and community-based conservation efforts, RESEEDPH will contribute to poverty reduction and increased resilience of vulnerable groups. Strengthened governance and inclusive policies will empower local stakeholders to engage in decision-making processes, ensuring equity in resource distribution and project benefits.

To reverse land degradation in forest and agrobiodiverse landscapes and enhance ecosystem resilience by improving soil health, restoring degraded areas, and strengthening the sustainability of rural production systems while generating significant biodiversity co-benefits.
